name: Road Trip Car Checklist
description: A checklist for preparing your car before a road trip.

items.text: Check engine oil level and condition; change it if a service is due.
Verify coolant level when cold and that it suits the climate ahead.
items.note: Long highway driving in heat raises engine temperatures — coolant matters.

items.text: Top up windshield washer fluid for bug and grime removal.
Check brake, power steering and transmission fluid levels.
Inspect belts and hoses for cracks, fraying or leaks.
Look under the car for any fresh fluid leaks.
Set all tire pressures to the door-jamb spec, allowing for a loaded car.
Check tread depth and look for cuts, bulges or uneven wear.
Confirm the spare is inflated and the jack and tools are present.
items.note: Know how to change a tire safely before you rely on the spare.

items.text: Verify lug nuts are tight and the TPMS light is off.
Consider a tire rotation or alignment if wear is uneven.
Pack a tire inflator or sealant for minor punctures.
Confirm the brake pedal is firm and braking is straight and quiet.
Have brakes inspected if you hear grinding or feel pulsing.
Check the parking brake holds on a slope.
Verify the steering is centered with no pulling or vibration.
Confirm ABS and brake warning lights are off.
Listen for suspension clunks over bumps.
Test headlights, high beams, brake lights and turn signals.
Check reverse, fog and hazard lights.
Replace worn wiper blades and fill washer fluid.
Clean the windshield, mirrors and headlights inside and out.
Confirm the defroster and demister clear the glass.
Pack spare bulbs and fuses if your car uses serviceable ones.
Pack jumper cables or a portable jump starter.
Carry a flashlight with spare batteries and a warning triangle.
Stock a first-aid kit and any personal medications.
Bring drinking water, snacks and weather-appropriate supplies.
Pack basic tools, gloves, a tow strap and duct tape.
Keep a phone charger, power bank and printed backup directions.
Confirm your insurance, registration and roadside assistance are current.
Fill the fuel tank or plan charging stops along the route.
Adjust mirrors, seat and headrest before you set off.
Test the horn, climate control and infotainment.
Secure cargo so nothing shifts or blocks visibility.
Do a final walkaround for tires, lights and fluid leaks.

faq.q: What is a road trip car checklist?
faq.a: It's a pre-trip inspection that prepares your car for a long drive — fluids, tires, brakes, lights and an emergency kit — so drivers catch faults before departure rather than on the side of a highway.

faq.q: When should I check my car before a road trip?
faq.a: Run the checklist several days before you leave so there is time to book a service or buy parts if needed. Do a final quick walkaround the morning of departure to confirm tires, lights and fluids.

faq.q: What should be in a road trip emergency kit?
faq.a: Carry a spare tire and tools, jumper cables or a jump pack, a flashlight, warning triangle, first-aid kit, water, basic tools, and weather-appropriate items. Add a phone charger and printed route or maps as backup.

faq.q: Should I get my car serviced before a long trip?
faq.a: If a service is due or close, do it before you go. For any leak, warning light or unusual noise, have a qualified mechanic inspect the car before a long drive rather than risk a breakdown away from home.

faq.q: Is this available as a printable PDF?
faq.a: Yes. Print the road trip car checklist to work through in the driveway, or download the PDF to complete on your phone before you set off.
